Application Materials.content:
**Applicants should scan and submit the following documents to the Online Application System for evaluation of their applications:**
- Identity documents (e.g. Identity card*, passport or other travel document)
- Official Transcript (for academic qualifications of undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies):
- An official final transcript for a completed programme
- The latest transcript if the programme is not yet completed
- An official English-translated copy must be attached if the transcript is not in English. The interpretation of grades (in English) is also required.
- Degree Certificate/Graduation Certificate/Proof of Study (as appropriate)
- Verification proof by third-party authorities (for a completed programme):
- Online Verification Report of Higher Education Degree Certificate (中國高等教育學位在綫驗証報告), both Chinese and English versions, issued by the CHSI (中國高等教育學生信息網) for qualification(s) awarded by universities in the Chinese Mainland
- Online Query of Overseas Credentials Evaluation Reports國(境)外學歷學位認証書 issued by the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) (教育部留學服務中心) (applicable to applicants from the Chinese Mainland with qualifications awarded by overseas universities)
- Proof of English language proficiency, e.g. IETLS, TOEFL, CET-6 Score Report (applicable to applicants whose degree, or exceptionally, an alternative qualification deemed equivalent, was not awarded by a tertiary institution where English was used as the MOI for the degree programme)
- Personal statement
- Reference letters (if any)
*Do not upload copy of HKID. Local students will be required to present HKID for verification upon registration.*
Applicants may be required to submit a Report for Qualifications Assessment issued by the Hong Kong Council for Accreditation of Academic & Vocational Qualifications (HKCAAVQ) to support their application.

Interview Requirements.content: For CET-6 results submitted for admission purposes, applicants must also demonstrate **competency in spoken English** through an **oral interview conducted by the Programme** and/or obtain grade B or above in the CET-6 Speaking English Test.

Application Deadlines.content: **Application Period:** Application starts from **1 October 2025** and will close on **30 June 2026**.

Academic Requirements.content: - **General Qualifications:** An applicant should hold a **bachelor's degree awarded by a recognized tertiary institution** or have **equivalent qualifications**, which will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: A recent GMAT or GRE test score, while not required, will be helpful in determining admittance into the Programme.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Proof of English proficiency is required for applicants whose Bachelor's degree was obtained from non-English medium institution, applicants must meet one of the following requirements:
- a **minimum score of 79 in TOEFL Internet-Based Test**; or
- a **band score of 6.0 or above in IELTS**; or
- a **minimum score of 450 or above in College English Test Band 6 (CET-6)**, with proof of competency in spoken English.
For IELTS and TOEFL qualifications for admission purposes, the University accepts only results from a **single test sitting**. The test must be **conducted at a recognised test centre** and **fall within the two-year validity period**, counted from the date of submission of the admission application for the specific intake cohort.
For CET-6 results submitted for admission purposes, the University accepts only those **obtained within the five-year validity period**, counted from the date of submission of the admission application for the specific intake cohort. Applicants must also demonstrate **competency in spoken English** through an oral interview conducted by the Programme and/or obtain grade B or above in the CET-6 Speaking English Test.
Applicants who **do not fulfil the above language requirements** but have an equivalent score in a recognized test, or an equivalent qualification assessment to prove their English language proficiency may be **considered on a case-by-case basis**.

Program Overview.content:
**Programme Information**
- Award Title: **Master of Science in Risk, Insurance and Actuarial Analytics Degree** **(MSc in RIAA)**
- Intermediate Award: Postgraduate Diploma in Risk, Insurance and Actuarial Analytics (PD in RIAA)
- Study Mode: Full-Time
- Duration: Normal: 1 year; Maximum: 2 years
**Special Features**
- The degree gives a broad and in-depth coverage of the major areas in risk management, insurance and actuarial science with an emphasis on professional practice.
- The degree helps students obtain professional qualifications such as Chartered Insurance Institute (CII), Financial Risk Manager (FRM) and actuarial science related qualifications, e.g. Associate of the Society of Actuaries (ASA) / Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA).
- Combining finance, economics, computer science and quantitative skills training, the degree offers a comprehensive understanding of risk and insurance, thereby enhancing the degree's attractiveness to both students and potential employers.
- The program provides students with opportunities to gain access to an extensive network of alumni and industry professionals and benefit from dedicated career services, including job placement, resume workshops and interview preparation.
**Learning Outcomes**
- Explain the theories and practices of risk management, insurance and actuarial science;
- Devise suitable risk management and actuarial strategies for different individuals and corporations;
- Demonstrate a mastery of quantitative skills in applying risk and actuarial models and performing risk analysis;
- Apply risk and actuarial analytics and insurance products to control risk exposures; and
- Explain regulatory compliance and regulations for insurance businesses in the insurance market.
**Career Destination**
Career opportunities include positions in insurance companies, banks, and other related financial institutions. MPhil or PhD Programmes are also options.

Cost of Attendance.content:
It is recommended that students prepare a budget of HK$6,200 - $7,500 to cover their first month's expenses.
The estimated monthly expenses may vary depending on individual lifestyle and spending habits. The following table is provided for general reference only:
| Item | Approx. expenses per month (HKD) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals (on campus) | HK$4,500 - $5,000 |
| Entertainment | HK$600 - $700 |
| Transportation (local) | HK$600 - $800 |
| Miscellaneous | HK$500 - $1,000 |
| **Total** | **HK$6,200 - $7,500** |

Financial Aid.content: **Academic Scholarship** Scholarships might be considered for outstanding students on the basis of academic merit.

Multiple Applications.content: You are required to submit separate applications if you wish to make multiple applications for different programmes of our School. Please also note that multiple application fees should be paid. Your chance of success will not be affected. However, applicants are not encouraged to switch to another programme once an admission offer has been accepted. Please be aware that the deposit fee will not be refunded if you decide to switch to another programme.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
An applicant who has been offered admission to an approved programme of study is required to register with the Programme Office on a specified date and is considered to have been admitted to such programme on the date of his/her first registration. Registration includes payment of the fees due and enrolment and selection of courses/sections. An applicant who fails to pay the prescribed fees or register on the relevant specified dates is considered as having forgone his/her place offered by the University.
A student who for special reasons seeks permission for deferment of his/her registration may apply in writing to the Programme Director **at least one week before the specified date for registration**. A fee for late registration will be charged by the Programme Office.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Applicants **with no or limited background** related to insurance and statistics in their first degree, or equivalent academic qualification, will have to complete and **pass pre-entry courses** prior to the start of this programme.
Applicants who **do not fulfil the above language requirements** but have an equivalent score in a recognized test, or an equivalent qualification assessment to prove their English language proficiency may be **considered on a case-by-case basis**.
